story_type: jump jet hovers and lands vertically on an amphibious assault ship at sea, squadron farewell tour
hook: This jet stopped in midair over a warship at sea.
narration: This jet stopped in midair over a warship at sea, then sat straight down on it.
It was a Marine Corps AV-8B Harrier from the Tomcats squadron, over the Coral Sea.
Four swiveling nozzles point the engine's thrust straight down, so a Harrier can hover with no runway at all.
The pilot balances the jet on that column of thrust, just above the deck.
It held there, hanging over the flight deck.
This was the squadron's farewell tour. The ship was trading its Harriers for the F-35B.
outcome: The Harrier settled onto the deck of the amphibious assault ship USS Bonhomme Richard.

location_card.place: Coral Sea, aboard USS Bonhomme Richard

title: Harrier hovers, then lands on a warship
description:
On Aug. 16, 2017, an AV-8B Harrier II from Marine Attack Squadron 311 performed vertical short takeoff and landing operations from the amphibious assault ship USS Bonhomme Richard in the Coral Sea, during the squadron's farewell tour before the ship's move to the F-35B.

Footage: U.S. Navy video by Mass Communication Specialist 2nd Class Diana Quinlan, via Wikimedia Commons: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:AV-8B_Harrier_II_Ops_Aboard_USS_Bonhomme_Richard.webm
